questions.q: What does Mandela's life suggest is the true path to freedom?
a: Education
Military resistance
Political alliances
Personal wealth
questions.why: The first lesson says Mandela recognized from the start of his education that learning was the real route to freedom.

questions.q: How did Mandela challenge authority at Fort Hare College?
a: He helped freshmen elect their own committee and threatened to resign
He organized a boycott of the college dining hall
He wrote a protest letter to the national government
He refused to sit his final examinations
questions.why: The second lesson describes the freshmen electing their own committee and threatening to resign if the warden overruled them.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the people history remembers?
a: We remember those who challenge the norm, not quiet followers
We remember those who held the highest public offices
We remember those who avoided conflict whenever possible
We remember those with the most formal education
questions.why: The second lesson says we do not remember yes-men but the rebels and troublemakers who challenged what was normal.

questions.q: What happened to Mandela after his 1964 treason conviction?
a: He was sentenced to life and kept learning and resisting
He was exiled and organized the movement from abroad
He was released after serving a short sentence
He was pardoned and immediately became president
questions.why: He received life in prison and spent 26 years there, continuing to educate himself and challenge authority.

questions.q: What did Mandela's protest about the prison shorts demonstrate?
a: He kept challenging authority even behind bars
He rejected every item of clothing the guards issued
He wanted uniforms reserved for political prisoners
He was demanding solitary confinement instead
questions.why: The third lesson says he objected that shorts were indecent for African men, and after two weeks of resistance the guards gave in.
